title: King Shibi and the Dove
text:
King Shibi was known through the world for his righteousness. To test him, the gods took animal form: Agni as a dove and Indra as a hawk. The dove, chased by the hawk, flew into the king's lap and begged for protection. Shibi promised it.

The hawk then spoke. It said the dove was its rightful food, that it was starving, and that a king who took away a creature's food was doing it a wrong too. Shibi offered the hawk any other meat it wanted, a bull or a boar, anything except the bird who had come to him for refuge. The hawk refused. It would accept only one thing: flesh from the king's own body, equal in weight to the dove.

Shibi agreed. A pair of scales was brought, and he put the dove on one side and began cutting flesh from his own body and placing it on the other. However much he cut, the dove remained heavier. At last the king climbed onto the scale himself, offering his whole body. At that the two gods revealed themselves, praised his steadfastness, and restored him.
lesson: A promise to protect someone is tested exactly when keeping it becomes expensive. If you are not willing to pay the cost, do not make the promise.
people: King Shibi, Agni as a dove, Indra as a hawk
caveat: The Mahabharata contains more than one version of the tale, with different gods and details.
